hypothesis: The parent ends every episode with each circuit pinned to one rule-consistent table, but many pins rest on the inventory-split coupling rather than on the circuit's own answers (e.g. i228 B: 2 rows observed, 16 tables fit its own answers; i81 C: 2 rows, 16; i209/i253 B: 3 rows, 9), and ~7 of 18 queries go unused. Spending the leftover budget on model-chosen checks that target exactly those coupling-only inferences will (a) leave every final unchanged when the rules reading is right, and (b) catch and repair a wrong deduction when it is not. Falsifiable: if any check answer ever disagrees with a deduced table, the parent's reading of the rules is wrong on that instance and its final would have been wrong.
behavior_changes: When no query can split the remaining rule-consistent candidates, querying no longer stops: the model is shown the deduced tables (with how many outputs were observed directly) and a menu of CHECK queries, and picks one; off-menu replies are re-asked as before.

Check menu order: first the rows where the circuit's own rule-allowed tables (two binary gates of types the inventory has, NOTs up to the total, ignoring how the inventory is split) still disagree with the deduction, ranked by how many such tables the row would rule out; only when none remain, any row of a pinned circuit not yet observed, least-observed circuit first.

Graded fallback when answers contradict the joint rules: per circuit, first the rule-allowed tables ignoring the inventory split, then any non-constant table (the parent jumped straight to any non-constant table, i.e. up to 254 candidates). Normal splitting queries then resume on that space.
During the check phase the state text says 'deduced table ... (k of 8 outputs observed directly)' instead of 'SOLVED ... Do NOT query again'.
preserved_behaviors: Frozen solver and label-free: only self.llm and env.query; the model writes every query; audit.py --arm scratch: OK.

Same hypothesis-space enumeration, joint inventory coupling, candidate listing, entropy-ranked split menu, veto/re-ask of zero-information replies, and final assembly from the model's per-circuit picks among consistent candidates (which already overrode the model's mis-typed 24 bits on i228).
Split phase is unchanged: on all 10 instances the queries before the first check are identical to the parent's.
verification: Audited the parent with an independent enumerator (formula trees op1(xi, op2(xj, xk)) with NOTs at all 5 positions, not the parent's signal-stack recursion), using only the .md/.json histories and system prompts (no gold fields): on all 10 b1 instances each final circuit is the unique joint-consistent table, so the enumerations agree; it also showed which circuits were pinned only via the coupling (per-circuit candidates 2-16 for several).

Offline fake-env test with a scripted first-menu-item model: two rule-consistent instances keep the right final; an off-rules circuit (XOR-like table under AND3/OR3) is contradicted by a check, falls back, and is recovered within the budget.
Ran check_b1r0_cand_pilot_strict_b10g3r2_b1r0g2.py: 10/10 status=ok, parsed_final_guess=True, queries_used=18 on every instance, 19-27 solver calls.

Read the results: 73 check-phase calls (4 re-asks); 0 of the extra check answers contradict the deduced tables; all 10 finals identical to the parent's; after the checks, every circuit on every instance is unique among its own rule-allowed tables WITHOUT the inventory coupling (independent enumerator), with 5-7 of 8 rows observed directly per circuit.

There was only one active branch in b1, so there were no cross-branch disagreements to adjudicate; the audit was of the parent's claimed 'SOLVED' states against an independent enumeration and against fresh answers.
risks: On this batch the gain is corroboration, not changed answers: the parent's finals were already the unique rule-consistent tables, and the checks confirmed them. The fallback/recovery path was exercised only in the offline fake test, not on a real instance.
More solver calls per episode (~19-27 vs ~8-17) and all 18 queries spent; if a metric penalises queries or tokens, this is a cost.
If a check does contradict a deduction late in the budget, the loose fallback may leave several candidates and the final then depends on the model's pick among them.
